open_points.subject: M08 AdmissionVerdict identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict” conflicts with “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions”; the new TrialExecutions have freshly minted identities.
open_points.question: When admission is repeated for the same implementation and unchanged corpus, is the prior AdmissionVerdict reused, is a new verdict entity created, or is the deterministic verdict value separate from the newly created execution evidence?
options: Reuse the existing verdict and do not create new TrialExecutions
Create a new AdmissionVerdict entity for every admission run
Keep one content-derived verdict value and record each admission run and its TrialExecutions separately
open_points.default_guess: Keep the deterministic verdict value separate from a distinct admission-run record containing the fresh TrialExecutions.

open_points.subject: M17 ProofResult identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result” conflicts with the carried decision that a version whose proof failed because a binding was proposed may be proven again after that same binding becomes accepted.
open_points.question: What facts determine a ProofResult’s identity when proof of an unchanged flow version can change as an OperationBinding changes status?
options: ProofResult is identified only by flow_version_id and may change in place
Each proof computation is a separate observation entity
ProofResult is a value identified by the flow version plus the relevant dependency state or by its complete result facts
open_points.default_guess: Treat ProofResult as a computed value whose meaning includes the binding state used by that proof.

open_points.subject: M07 TrialExecution and M08 AdmissionVerdict provenance
open_points.text: K-15 says “The owner's actions, each agent's and the kernel's own are distinguishable in every record,” but TrialExecution has no requester or actor, and AdmissionVerdict has no actor even though trials may be requested by an agent or created as part of kernel-run admission.
open_points.question: Which actor facts must distinguish an agent-requested trial from an admission trial, and how is the kernel recorded as the actor deciding an AdmissionVerdict?
options: Record both the requesting actor and whether the execution belongs to an admission
Record only an executing actor, using the agent for direct trials and the kernel for admission trials
Treat all TrialExecutions and AdmissionVerdicts as kernel observations and do not retain the requesting actor
open_points.default_guess: Record the requester and execution purpose on TrialExecution, and record the kernel as the AdmissionVerdict’s deciding actor.

open_points.subject: Agent submission of personal_data
open_points.text: State 0 says the owner “is the only reader of personal data” and that personal-data values “reach an agent only as digest and class,” while “run a flow” is available to an agent and M19 places no actor restriction on supplying a flow input whose port declares personal_data; authored trial cases similarly accept values without an ingress restriction.
open_points.question: May an agent submit an actual personal_data value as a run input, flow constant, or authored trial-case value, or must such value-bearing actions be owner-only?
options: Reject personal-data payloads supplied by agents
Allow agents to supply personal-data payloads but never return those payloads to them
Allow agents to supply only an opaque service reference or digest, not the value
open_points.default_guess: Allow agent-supplied values because the stated disclosure rule governs values returned by the kernel, while continuing to redact every personal-data value in responses.

open_points.subject: TrialCase and file-fixture inspection
open_points.text: K-12 says a repairing agent receives “that slot's recent traces and trial evidence,” but M06 says TrialCase is read only “by trial and admission,” and no text says whether the agent or owner may read its input values or durable file-fixture bytes.
open_points.question: What parts of TrialCases, including file fixtures, are returned to a repairing agent or through inspection, and how does disclosure class affect that read?
options: Return non-personal values and fixture bytes to agents, redacting personal_data to digest and class
Return only case metadata and digests to agents; fixture bytes are owner-only
Return TrialExecutions to agents but never TrialCase inputs or fixture bytes
open_points.default_guess: Return non-personal TrialCase values and fixture bytes to an authorized repairing agent, with personal_data represented only by digest and class.

open_points.subject: M28 owner_token and agent_tokens
open_points.text: The text requires unique agent names and constant-time token comparison but is silent on whether the owner token and all agent-token credential values must be mutually unique.
open_points.question: What happens if the same token value is configured for the owner and an agent, or for two differently named agents, when one request must mint exactly one Actor identity?
options: Reject configuration unless every owner and agent token value is globally unique
Apply a fixed matching precedence such as owner before agents
Allow one token to identify multiple configured actors and require another request attribute to disambiguate
open_points.default_guess: Reject startup or token-list reload when any configured owner or agent token value is duplicated.
